text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Simposium on Croatian foreign policy concludes that Croatia belongs to Europe, but will be a hostage to nobody's policies.
- Croatian and Yugoslav foreign ministers to sign a consular convention and an accord on legal aid.
- President Tudjman awards former foreign ministers of Germany and Hungary and former chairman of the contact group for former Yugoslavia for special merits.
- American corporation Bechtel is still negotiating on the construction of the Zagreb-Split motorway, says its vice presiden Charles Redman.
- Croatian banks began extending long-awaited loans for car purchases with colateral in real estate.
- Marinas on the Adriatic which are owned by shipping companies should be nationalised, says state counsel Petar Sale.
- Polls show current president Franjo Tudjman may win sufficient majority of up to 57 percent votes in the first round of presidential elections due in mid June.
- Croatia Airlines will use a leased Airbus this summer to improve links with Europe, says its director Ivan MIsetic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
